title: Worms and Snakes: Animals We Love to Hate
main_content:
They slither. They are slimy.

They are worms and snakes. From ancient folk stories to modern animated films, snakes and worms do not often play the hero.

This is also true in American English.

If you don’t like worms, one is bad enough. But a whole can of worms is really bad! “A can of worms” is a very difficult issue or set of problems.

Now, worms are good at slowly digging themselves into the ground. This is the root of common expressions.

If you “worm your way into something”, you get something you want by slowly using tricks and lies. For example, “I can’t believe he wormed his way back into her life! She won’t ever learn!”

When snakes move, they slither along the ground or in the grass. So, “a snake in the grass” is a sneaky person who cannot be trusted.

Another reason many people fear snakes is because they bite. So, snakebit means to be very unlucky. For example, if your favorite soccer team is “snakebit”, they are losing every game.

questions.question: How can you call a sneaky person?
If you were using tricks or lies to get what you wanted what would you be doing?
If someone is very unlucky what do you say about that person?
